answer: Brahms-style peer sampling keeps sybils from eclipsing agents. Each agent holds sampler slots that retain the peer ID minimizing a private keyed hash, so a zephyr of fake pushes cannot bias picks beyond the swarm's true ID share. Each sender's pushes are capped at a narrow ledge per round, and if total pushes exceed the expected rate the round is discarded. Pulled views must echo the responder's own samples, letting agents spot views stuffed with one cluster.
